SP/FA MT1 [Octa 2]

Reading

Choose the correct answer.

U1 L1

In 1602, John came to America from England. He met a Native American. His name was Running Bear. John never met a Native American before. It was the first time. The two boys talked about their names.

“Running Bear? That’s an interesting name. Who named you?” asked John.

“Our chief named me when I was born. He names all the people in our village,” said Running Bear.

“Wow! Does everyone have that kind of name?”

“Yes. Our names are common words like Large Tree and Stars.”

“They’re different from ours. We use special words like Matthew and Amy. And parents usually name their children.”

“Do your names change as you grow up?”

“No, our names don’t change.”

“Really? Ours do.”
1. What is the passage mainly about?
A)differences between names
B)when Running Bear got his name
C)the lives of Native American boys
D)how John and Running Bear became friends
2. What is true about John in 1602?
A)He was not in America.
B)He met a chief in the village.
C)He changed his name.
D)He left England.
3. Who names the people in Native American villages?
A)the parents
B)Running Bear
C)Native American children
D)the chief
4. How are Native American names different from English names?
A)Native American names are special words like Matthew and Amy.
B)Native American names are common words like Running Bear.
C)Native American names come from their parents.
D)Native American names do not change.
5. What does the underlined sentence mean?
A)We like special words.
B)Our names are not common words.
C)It is easy to understand our names.
D)We change our names into special words.

U1 L2

John was an American soldier. One day, he saw a Native American when he walked through the trees. He had long, black hair and brown eyes. He wore animal hides.

“Hello, I'm John,” said John.
“Hello,” said the Native American. “I am Kicking Bird.”
“How did you get that name?” asked John.
“I got it from the chief. He names all the children in our village,” said Kicking Bird.

Kicking Bird invited John to his village. In the village, he met other Native Americans and became friends. When John was taking a walk with them, a wolf suddenly showed up. Surprisingly, the wolf came along and looked at him. John felt there was something special between them. He touched it softly. They ran and played together. The chief saw them from far away. He thought they were dancing together. The chief named John “Dances with Wolves.”

*soldier 군인    **hide (동물의) 가죽    ***show up 나타나다
1. What is NOT true about Kicking Bird?
A)He was an American soldier.
B)He had long, black hair.
C)He wore animal hides.
D)He got his name from the chief.
2. Where did Kicking Bird invite John?
A)to his village
B)to America
C)to the trees
D)to the soldier's village
3. Why did the chief give John a new name?
A)John was a good soldier.
B)John talked with the wolf.
C)John looked like he was dancing with the wolf.
D)John was good at dancing.
4. What does the underlined sentence mean?
A)John suddenly met a wolf while he was walking.
B)The wolf suddenly walked away.
C)John and the wolf were taking a walk together.
D)John suddenly showed up with a wolf.

U2 L1

Over the years, London has found many solutions to its traffic problems.

The 1800s: Going Underground
London's roads were full of horses and wagons. They made the roads very crowded. In 1863, the city opened the Tube, the world's first underground railway. Many people went underground and took the Tube. The roads became less busy.

The 1900s: Two Buses in One
There were many buses on the roads. And they were packed with people. So London made a double-decker bus in 1923. It carried more people and saved road space.

The 2000s: Paying to Drive
The roads had too many cars. People were tired of heavy traffic. In 2003, the city introduced a new law. It said drivers had to pay to drive during busy hours. This helped lower the traffic level.
1. What is the passage mainly about?
A)how to solve traffic problems in London
B)how many different buses are on the roads
C)how people made the Tube
D)why drivers pay in London
2. What happened after they opened the Tube?
A)Many people did not like it.
B)The roads were still crowded.
C)There was not a lot of traffic.
D)People had to pay money to drive.
3. What is true about the double-decker bus?
A)It went underground.
B)It saved space on the roads.
C)Only tourists rode it.
D)It made roads more crowded.
4. What was the main traffic problem in the 2000s?
A)not enough buses
B)a lot of cars on the road
C)many people on the Tube
D)many horses and wagons
5. What might we know about London?
A)There may be a lot of people in London.
B)People like busy streets.
C)Buses are not on the roads.
D)Some people still use horses and wagons.
